target: AG1's claim that a national Election Day holiday would broadly remove scheduling barriers to voting.
objection: A federal holiday would not reliably give many schedule-constrained voters, especially low-income retail and service workers employed by private employers, paid time off or guaranteed time away from work, so the main barrier could remain.

target: AG1's claim that lowering scheduling barriers through a holiday would increase turnout and strengthen democracy.
objection: Research shows that an election holiday by itself is not an effective way to increase voter turnout compared with other voting-access reforms, so the turnout gains are likely overstated.

target: AG1's assumption that broad holiday observance makes a federal Election Day holiday a reliable solution for low-income workers.
objection: Because private employers are not required to provide paid holiday leave, many low-income workers in retail and service jobs would still have to work and could even face lost wages, so the holiday may not meaningfully help them vote.

target: AG1's claim that making voting a holiday would meaningfully increase civic participation through symbolic framing.
objection: Even if a holiday changes civic framing, it will not reliably translate into real voting time for many workers without guaranteed paid time off, so the symbolic effect is insufficient on its own.

target: AG1's argument that holiday observance broadly creates usable non-working time for schedule-constrained voters.
objection: Federal holidays do not require private employers to close or give guaranteed time off, and many retail and service employers still schedule shifts on holidays, so the holiday would not reliably eliminate time conflicts for many workers.

target: AG1's claim that a federal holiday would remove major scheduling barriers for low-income workers in particular.
objection: Low-income workers are among the most constrained by job and wage pressures, and because their holiday work schedules may remain unchanged, the policy would fail to reliably increase access for the voters who need the biggest barrier removal.

target: AG1's claim that federal holiday observance through school closures and reduced workplace schedules would reliably free time for voting.
objection: School closures and partial workplace reductions do not reliably eliminate the core scheduling barrier if the most constrained low-income workers still must work holiday shifts, so the holiday does not reliably solve their time-conflict problem.

target: AG1's preference for a national holiday over other reforms.
objection: More reliable alternatives exist, such as state laws that enforce employer time off for voting and automatic voter registration, which directly target voting barriers instead of depending on voluntary holiday observance.
